easystats support for bmmfit objects

Source: R/easystats-insight.R
easystats-bmmfit.Rd

These S3 methods let the insight package, and through it the easystats packages parameters, bayestestR and modelbased, read a bmm fit as the model you specified with bmm(): its parameters, their formulas, the response variables and the data, rather than the brms model that bmm builds from them. With them, for example, parameters::model_parameters() and bayestestR::describe_posterior() summarise each model parameter in its own component, and for models such as sdm(), modelbased::estimate_means(fit, by = "set_size", predict = "c") returns the estimates of a model parameter on its native scale.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'bmmfit'
find_formula(x, verbose = TRUE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bmmfit'
find_predictors(
  x,
  effects = "fixed",
  component = "all",
  flatten = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'bmmfit'
find_response(x, combine = TRUE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bmmfit'
get_data(
  x,
  effects = "all",
  component = "all",
  source = "frame",
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'bmmfit'
find_parameters(
  x,
  effects = "all",
  component = "all",
  flatten = FALSE,
  parameters = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'bmmfit'
get_priors(x, verbose = TRUE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bmmfit'
model_info(x, response = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bmmfit'
link_function(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bmmfit'
link_inverse(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A bmmfit object (created by bmm()).

...

Ignored, for consistency with the generics.

effects

"fixed" for the population-level part of the model, "random" for the group-level part or "all" for both: coefficients for find_parameters(), predictors for find_predictors(), columns for get_data(). find_parameters() also takes "full", "random_variance" and "grouplevel", as the methods of insight for brms fits do.

component

"all", "conditional", "location", "distributional" or "auxiliary", which all select every model parameter, or for find_parameters() the name of a model parameter; ignored by get_data().

flatten

Should a character vector be returned instead of a list?

combine, source, verbose

Ignored, for consistency with the generics.

parameters

A regular expression the names of the returned parameters must match.

response

Ignored, for consistency with the generic.

Value

See the insight generics, e.g. insight::find_formula() and insight::find_parameters().

Details

Each method reshapes what the fit already stores:

  • find_formula() returns one formula per model parameter, and per helper parameter of a non-linear formula, with the population-level and group-level parts as separate elements (<parameter> and <parameter>_random), plus a conditional formula of the response variables on all population-level predictors.

  • find_predictors() returns the predictors of these formulas: the population-level predictors for effects = "fixed", the grouping factors for "random" and both for "all". Every model parameter counts as both a location and a distributional parameter, so each component returns the same variables.

  • find_response() returns the names of the response columns, as get_data() returns them.

  • get_data() returns the data the model was fitted to as you passed them: without the columns bmm adds for its own use or brms computes from the formula (such as ID:session or log(x)), and with the response categories of a model fitted to counts (e.g. m3()) as columns of their own. The model frame stored in the fit is always the source; source is ignored.

  • find_parameters() returns the names of the posterior draws in one element per model parameter (<parameter> for the population-level coefficients, <parameter>_random for the group-level ones), without the parameters that the brms family needs but the model does not have, such as the fixed mu of the response-time models. component selects a model parameter by name; "all", "conditional", "location", "distributional" and "auxiliary" select all of them. insight::get_parameters() and insight::clean_parameters() build on it.

  • get_priors() returns one row per population-level coefficient, group-level standard deviation and correlation, with the prior that applies to it. A parameter fixed to a constant has the distribution "constant" and the constant as its location.

  • model_info() describes the model as not linear and as having no dispersion parameter; the family is the one of the brms model.

  • link_function() and link_inverse() return the link function of the first parameter that has one and its inverse. bmm models have one link per parameter, so for anything else use model$links.

See also

insight::find_formula(), insight::find_parameters(), insight::get_priors()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
insight::find_formula(fit)
parameters::model_parameters(fit)
bayestestR::describe_posterior(fit)
modelbased::estimate_means(fit, by = "set_size", predict = "c")
} # }
